content_html:
A refurbished iPad can be one of the better-value ways to buy an Apple tablet, especially if you do not need the newest model. The difficulty is that eBay has everything from low-cost older iPads to recent M-series models, and the cheapest listing is not always the best buy.

This guide focuses on five iPads that still make sense for US buyers in 2026. We have prioritized useful performance, sensible features, availability on eBay and the likelihood that the tablet will remain enjoyable to use for several years rather than simply choosing the lowest advertised price.

Price snapshot: when we checked current eBay.com listings in September 2026, examples ranged from roughly $165 for a refurbished 9th-generation iPad 64GB to around $288 for an iPad Air 5 64GB, around $300 for a 10th-generation iPad with cellular, around $359 for an iPad mini 6 64GB, and roughly $575 for an M1 11-inch iPad Pro 256GB. These are examples rather than guaranteed prices: storage, cosmetic grade, Wi-Fi versus cellular, warranty and seller can change the price substantially.

Quick answer: which refurbished iPad should you buy?

  • Best overall value: iPad Air 5th generation.
  • Best for families and everyday use: iPad 10th generation.
  • Best for power users: 11-inch iPad Pro 3rd generation (M1).
  • Best compact choice: iPad mini 6th generation.
  • Best budget choice: iPad 9th generation.

1. iPad Air 5th generation — best overall refurbished iPad

The fifth-generation iPad Air is the model we would check first for most buyers. Its Apple M1 chip gives it far more performance headroom than many older standard iPads, while the 10.9-inch design is light enough to work well as a sofa tablet, travel device, student machine or lightweight laptop replacement with a keyboard.

It also uses USB-C and supports the second-generation Apple Pencil, which makes the accessory experience cleaner than on older Lightning-based iPads. The main compromise is storage: the base model has 64GB, which can feel tight if you keep lots of games, downloaded video or large creative files on the device.

Who should buy it: buyers who want the strongest balance of performance, portability and price without paying iPad Pro money.

What to check: storage capacity, whether a charger is included, screen condition and whether you genuinely need cellular. A 256GB Wi-Fi model can be more useful long term than a cheaper 64GB cellular model for many buyers.

Compare current refurbished iPad Air 5 listings on eBay

2. iPad 10th generation — best for families and general use

The 10th-generation iPad is a strong mainstream choice if you mainly want web browsing, streaming, video calls, schoolwork, shopping, email and casual gaming. It moved the standard iPad to a more modern 10.9-inch design with USB-C, making it easier to share chargers and accessories with many newer devices.

Its performance is not as strong as the M1 iPad Air, but that does not matter much for everyday tablet use. In fact, a well-priced 10th-generation iPad can be the more sensible choice for a family device because you are not paying for power you may never use.

Who should buy it: households, students and casual users who want a modern-looking iPad at a lower cost than an Air or Pro.

What to check: Wi-Fi versus cellular, 64GB versus 256GB storage and accessory compatibility. Apple Pencil support is a little less straightforward on this model than on the Air 5, so check which Pencil you intend to use before buying accessories separately.

Compare current refurbished iPad 10th generation listings on eBay

3. 11-inch iPad Pro 3rd generation (M1) — best premium value

The 2021 11-inch iPad Pro is older on paper, but its M1 chip still gives it serious performance. It is the model to consider if you want a smoother 120Hz ProMotion display, stronger speakers, more capable cameras, Face ID and the flexibility of Apple's Pro accessories without buying a current-generation Pro at full retail pricing.

This is also the most interesting option for heavier multitasking, photo editing, illustration, music work or people who plan to connect the iPad to external displays and accessories. The catch is that used and refurbished Pro pricing varies dramatically. Storage, cellular capability and cosmetic grade can move the price by hundreds of dollars, so compare like-for-like configurations.

Who should buy it: buyers who will actually use the better display, higher performance or premium hardware.

What to check: battery condition, screen uniformity, storage, included charger, cellular status and whether the listing is for the 3rd-generation 11-inch M1 model rather than an older Intel-era Mac-style naming assumption. Read the full item specifics before buying.

Compare current refurbished 11-inch M1 iPad Pro listings on eBay

4. iPad mini 6th generation — best small iPad

The iPad mini 6 is still one of the most distinctive tablets Apple has made. Its 8.3-inch display makes it much easier to hold one-handed than a standard iPad, while the A15 Bionic chip provides capable performance for reading, travel, note-taking, games and media.

It also has USB-C and works particularly well for people who want a digital notebook or compact travel companion. The smaller screen is the whole point, but it is also the reason not to buy one: if you expect to spend hours using spreadsheets, split-screen apps or a keyboard case, a larger iPad is usually more comfortable.

Who should buy it: travelers, readers, pilots, commuters, note-takers and anyone who values portability above screen size.

What to check: 64GB versus 256GB storage, Wi-Fi versus cellular and the screen edges for impact damage. Because mini models can retain value well, compare the price with larger refurbished iPads before assuming the smaller tablet is automatically cheaper.

Compare current refurbished iPad mini 6 listings on eBay

5. iPad 9th generation — best budget refurbished iPad

If the goal is to spend as little as possible while still getting a capable iPad, the 9th-generation model deserves a look. It uses the older design with a Home button and Lightning connector, but it remains perfectly practical for streaming, browsing, children's apps, FaceTime, school portals and basic productivity.

The biggest reason to choose it is price. During our September 2026 check, we found current refurbished examples well below the prices of the Air, mini and Pro models. That makes the 9th-generation iPad particularly attractive as a first tablet, a shared family device or a secondary screen for around the house.

Who should buy it: budget-conscious buyers who care more about function than having the latest design.

What to check: 64GB versus 256GB storage, battery condition and whether you are happy to keep using Lightning accessories. If the price gets too close to a refurbished 10th-generation iPad, we would usually move up to the newer design instead.

Compare current refurbished iPad 9th generation listings on eBay

How much should you spend on a refurbished iPad?

There is no single correct price because eBay listings change constantly and the same iPad can be offered in several storage capacities, cosmetic grades and connectivity versions. A useful way to shop is to decide which model you want first, then compare at least five listings with the same storage and Wi-Fi or cellular specification.

Do not compare a 64GB Good-condition Wi-Fi model directly with a 256GB Excellent-condition cellular model. The headline price difference may be completely justified. Also check whether shipping is free and whether the seller offers free returns, because a slightly more expensive listing can still be the better overall deal.

What does eBay Refurbished condition mean?

Many qualifying eBay Refurbished listings are sold in condition grades such as Good, Very Good or Excellent. The cosmetic standard changes by grade, but the more important point is to read the listing rather than relying on the label alone. Look for clear information about testing, accessories, warranty and returns.

In several current listings we checked, eBay Refurbished products included a one-year warranty and some also offered free returns. Those protections can be worth paying a little more for compared with an untested used device from an unknown seller.

Seven checks before buying a refurbished iPad on eBay

  1. Check the exact generation. iPad names are repetitive, so verify the generation, model year and screen size.
  2. Compare the same storage capacity. A 256GB model should not be compared directly with a 64GB model.
  3. Confirm Wi-Fi or cellular. Cellular models may cost more, and unlocked status matters if you plan to add a data plan.
  4. Read the cosmetic description. A lower grade can be excellent value if you are happy with visible wear.
  5. Check seller feedback and sales history. A high-volume seller with strong recent feedback can be worth prioritizing over the absolute cheapest listing.
  6. Read the returns and warranty terms. These matter more on refurbished electronics than a small difference in purchase price.
  7. Check what is included. Do not assume an Apple charger, cable, Pencil or keyboard is included unless the listing says so.

Which refurbished iPad would we buy?

For most people, the iPad Air 5th generation is our first choice because the M1 chip, USB-C design and strong accessory support give it an unusually good balance of longevity and price. If you simply want an iPad for family use, streaming and everyday tasks, the 10th-generation iPad can be the smarter purchase when it is meaningfully cheaper.

At the low end, the 9th-generation iPad remains compelling when the saving is substantial. At the high end, the M1 11-inch iPad Pro is the model to watch if you want premium hardware and can find the right configuration at a sensible refurbished price. The iPad mini 6 is less about bargain hunting and more about buying the compact form factor because you specifically want it.

Guide checked and updated September 15, 2026. Prices, availability, seller terms and condition grades change frequently. Always check the live eBay listing before purchasing.
